title: PocketMap: lightweight lane anchors and telemetry affordances for console navigation
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Problem: The Redwood Console left rail has grown heavy with routes, project shortcuts, and cost/rollout surfaces. Customers report cognitive load when locating frequently used dashboards and unclear surface signals for rollout state and cost anomalies.

Goal: Deliver a low-risk, incremental redesign that introduces 'PocketMap' — a lightweight lane anchoring pattern plus telemetry affordances — to make rapid navigation, context discovery, and cost/latency signals visible without a full top-down IA rewrite. This ticket covers prototypes, engineering feasibility checks, and initial usability sessions for the left rail and workspace switch flow only.

Scope: left rail compact mode, lane anchors (micro landmarks), hover previews, route hinting (short descriptive badges), telemetry affordances (per-lane micro-metrics: cost delta, p95 latency, rollout health), and a lightweight workspace quick-jump. Explicitly out of scope: complete global IA changes, command palette overhaul, and tenant-level permission redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Prototype in Figma demonstrating compact rail with three lane anchors and hover previews for dashboard, rollouts, and cost views.
2) Usability test (n=5) showing median time-to-target reduced by >=20% for common tasks (open rollout, open cost dashboard, switch workspace).
3) Engineering spike scoped (ENG ticket created) to validate route aliasing, client-side route hints, and telemetry endpoints.
4) PM sign-off on rollout affordance language and wording for micro-metrics.
5) Accessibility review completed for keyboard and screenreader interactions.
comments: 2025-01-08 Ava Morales: Initial brief added after sync with PM. Sketches created for three candidate anchors: Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost. Figma seeds: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/PocketMap-seeds (private). Confluence spec: https://acme.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONS/pages/7654321-PocketMap-Overview

2025-01-09 Samir Patel: Reviewed sketches. Engineering concerns: route aliasing complexity and existing router middleware. Requested an engineering spike to estimate work. Created ENG-2045 as spike to validate route compatibility and telemetry wiring.

2025-01-10 Jordan Kim (PM): Added product constraints — the design must not change existing API routes or break deep links. Need explicit copy for rollout health states (Healthy / Degraded / Fallback).

2025-01-13 Research team (Dmitri Orlov): Quick hallway test (n=6) with prototype A/B (anchors vs no anchors). Early signal: anchors reduced scanning time but hover previews were missed by keyboard-only users. Recommend clearer focus states and persistent accessible labels.

2025-01-14 Design critique: Leah Ng (Eng Lead) — positive on telemetry affordances. Ask: can we back off from live micro-metrics and instead surface last-1h delta to avoid streaming costs? Action: add fallback 'stale' state and inexpensive sampling approach.

2025-01-16 Ava Morales: Updated Figma with compact and expanded anchor variants, added accessibility focus ring and keyboard jump (Alt+K) behaviour. New prototype: https://www.figma.com/proto/xyz789/PocketMap-proto

2025-01-17 Usability test plan uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1u2u3uPocketMap-tests. Tasks: open rollout, identify cost spike, switch to secondary workspace. Facilitator notes to capture time-to-target and confusion points.

2025-01-18 Samir Patel: ENG-2045 spike estimate: 3 dev days + 2 QA days to implement route alias mapping and lightweight metrics endpoint. Proposed approach: client-side route hints and server-side sampled metrics endpoint (low CPU). Created PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1420

2025-01-20 Ava Morales: Collated findings and updated ticket for in-review. Next steps: finalize copy for rollout micro-state, handoff to engineering (ENG-2101 for implementation), and schedule 2 design QA passes during sprint planning.
